newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHARES SEEN HIGHER AFTER THREE-SESSION DIP.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHARES SEEN HIGHER AFTER THREE-SESSION DIP.

text.p: Polish shares were expected to rebound on Wednesday after a three-session fall, signalled by Tuesday's stronger buying after price-fixing, but analysts were not convinced a significant growth trend was imminent.
They said concerns over recent flooding that swamped over one percent of the country and the run-up to the September 21 parliamentary elections should limit the market's upside.

Analysts also said Tuesday's news that the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) notified the public prosecutor that a group of investors may have illegally manipulated prices may also dim bourse sentiment.
But they said Kruszwica should benefit from Tuesday's news the Cereol unit of France's Eridania Beghin-Say reached an agreement to buy a 45 percent stake in the edible fats maker.
